newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: PSA sees 0.5 percent Euro car sales rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: PSA sees 0.5 percent Euro car sales rise in 1997.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen Chairman Jacques Calvet said the group was holding its estimate for a 0.5 percent rise this year in western European car sales despite a poor start to the year in France.
In the rest of Europe, excluding France, sales have been better than expected, rising four percent in January and February, he told reporters at the Geneva car show.
In January and February," what happened in France brings us to a weaker trend than foreseen," he said.
In the first two months of the year new car sales in France were down 29 percent. The group has forecast a 10 percent drop in France for the full year.
Calvet said the sharp decline is not unexpected given the expiry at the end of September of a state rebate programme that had supported the market.
He said he expected the severe after-effect to ease, but has so far not revised the French market forecast.
"The first two months in Europe were slightly better than we had foreseen," he said.

The group expects sales for western Europe excluding France to rise 2.5 percent in 1997, due largely to big gains in Italy this year. He said the rise in first two months of the year was four percent.

"This would bring us to a weak figure for Europe including France of around 0.5 percent for the year. For the moment our view of the contribution of France and the rest of Europe has changed but we have not made an overall revision," Calvet added.
